title: Which solid has a circle on top and rectangles at the front and side?
description: Three views are given, and the board finds the solid that makes them. It reads the most unusual view first, keeps only the solids that can show it, then checks the front view and the side view against the solid that is left.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the most unusual view first, then check the other two views against the solid. Watch for students who match the solid to only one of the three views.

source: Figure it Out (shadows and views, question 3)
video_script.why: The child names a solid from its top, front and side views by starting with the view that is most unusual.
video_script.substitution: Read the most unusual view first, list the solids that can show it, then test the other two views.
video_script.anchor: three frames for the top, front and side views, and five solids to choose from: a cylinder, a cone, a triangular prism, a square pyramid and a cube

final_answer.value: Read the most unusual view first, then check the other two against the solid; here the solid is a cylinder
final_answer.spoken: the solid is a cylinder; read the most unusual view first, then check the other two

hold_back: Answer: the solid is a cylinder
maths_rules: stand-in views: top view a circle; front view a rectangle; side view a rectangle
a circle in a view needs a round solid: of the five, only the cylinder and the cone
the cone shows a triangle from the front and the side; the cylinder shows a rectangle
a cylinder looks the same from every side, so the side view is a rectangle too
other sets: circle with triangles is a cone; triangle with rectangles is a triangular prism; square with diagonals and triangles is a square pyramid; three squares is a cube
video_script.design: Three frames show the given views. The five solids sit in a row; the ones that cannot show a circle fade, then the cone fades when the front view is read.
open_questions: The seven sets of views in the book question are pictures that are not in the extracted text, so the video works one set (a circle with two rectangles) and names the other pairings in the board notes.
